propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, in cujus passione, secundum Simeonis prophetiam, dulcissimam animam
gloriosae Virginis et Matris Mariae doloris gladius pertransivit: concede
propitius; ut, qui dolores ejus venerando recolimus, passionis tuae effectum
felicem consequamur: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre in unitate.

The 1962 wording was read on 2026-10-01 on that edition's page image at 200 and again at 400 dpi (printed p. 657, no. 3624, under the heading Sequentia with the rubric (in Missis votivis omittenda); artifact PDF p. 738, left and right columns), not on any text layer, and the string the 2026-09-04 backfill had stored and quarantined for recogniser damage was not used. Every word was then read on the 1862 Pustet at printed pp. 420-421; 541, Festum VII. Dolorum B. M. Virg. (Friday after Passion Sunday), Sequentia in Missis Votivis omittenda; and Dominica III. Septembris, In Festo VII. Dolorum B. M. Virginis, the rubric 'et post Sequentiam additur Alleluja', read on the page image of its registered facsimile PDF at pp. 506-507; 627 (text-layer address lines 59897-59977 and 59989-59995 and 74314-74324), which carries the text word for word. Differences from the antecedent: the 1862 prints the poem once, under its March formulary, and at the September feast (printed p. 541) directs that the Mass be said as there and that Alleluja be added after the Sequence; the trailing Alleluia of the 1962 is that rubric carried out; the 1862 spells lacrymosa, moerebat and inclyti where the 1962 spells lacrimosa, maerebat and incliti: two received spellings of each word; the 1862 prints Eja and Juxta, Jesum, jam, Judicii: the j orthography the calendar declares; the 1862 sets Natum, Nati and Cruce (Fac me cruce) in lower case and Judicii with a capital; the 1862 sets no comma after Eia, after Mater (Eja Mater fons), or after the Fac of three strophes, where the 1962 sets them; the 1962 sets each line of the strophe with an initial capital, as the 1862 also does; the calendar carries one strophe per line. Read on the 1962 page image at 200 and 400 dpi: identical to the 2364 setting of the Friday after Passion Sunday except for a comma after fleret, a comma after stare, and the closing Alleluia; the 1862 sets both of those commas too.

propers.name: Sequence
propers.text:
Stabat Mater dolorosa Juxta Crucem lacrimosa, Dum pendebat Filius.
Cujus animam gementem, Contristatam et dolentem, Pertransivit gladius.
O quam tristis et afflicta Fuit illa benedicta Mater Unigeniti!
Quae maerebat, et dolebat, Pia Mater, dum videbat Nati poenas incliti.
Quis est homo, qui non fleret, Matrem Christi si videret In tanto supplicio?
Quis non posset contristari, Christi Matrem contemplari Dolentem cum Filio?
Pro peccatis suae gentis Vidit Jesum in tormentis, Et flagellis subditum.
Vidit suum dulcem Natum Moriendo desolatum, Dum emisit spiritum.
Eia, Mater, fons amoris, Me sentire vim doloris Fac, ut tecum lugeam.
Fac, ut ardeat cor meum In amando Christum Deum, Ut sibi complaceam.
Sancta Mater, istud agas, Crucifixi fige plagas Cordi meo valide.
Tui Nati vulnerati, Tam dignati pro me pati, Poenas mecum divide.
Fac me tecum pie flere, Crucifixo condolere, Donec ego vixero.
Juxta Crucem tecum stare, Et me tibi sociare In planctu desidero.
Virgo virginum praeclara, Mihi jam non sis amara: Fac me tecum plangere.
Fac, ut portem Christi mortem, Passionis fac consortem, Et plagas recolere.
Fac me plagis vulnerari, Fac me Cruce inebriari, Et cruore Filii.
Flammis ne urar succensus, Per te, Virgo, sim defensus In die judicii.
Christe, cum sit hinc exire, Da per Matrem me venire Ad palmam victoriae.
Quando corpus morietur, Fac, ut animae donetur Paradisi gloria. Amen. Alleluia.

translations.caution:
A LITERARY TRANSLATION, CHOSEN AS A VOICE. Caswall, Neale, Aylward and Bute
differ materially over these five texts. The active overlay records the
maintainer's choice of Caswall as the through-line across all five and Irons as
an alternative for the Dies irae; it does not argue that either voice is right.

The English is metrical verse and is not a clause-for-clause rendering. Where the
Latin sets a short strophe Caswall may fold two into one six-line stanza, and the
stanza divisions in the text recorded here are his and not the Missal's. He
renders no Amen and no Alleluia anywhere: every one of these five propers ends in
the Latin with an acclamation that the English simply does not have.

The same transcription as the Friday-after-Passion-Sunday commemoration above, and this index reprints the Latin twice rather than referencing it once, so the English is recorded twice with it. The 15 September setting differs from the March one in the Latin -- a comma after `fleret` and after `stare`, and the ending `Paradisi gloria. Amen. Alleluia.` against `Paradisi gloria. Amen.` -- and NOT in anything the English renders; Caswall renders neither the Amen nor the Alleluia. If the two masses are ever joined by a `takes_from`, this row is the one to drop.
translations.source_label: Lyra Catholica: containing all the Breviary and Missal hymns, with others from various sources, translated by Edward Caswall (London: James Burns, 1849)
translations.text:
At the Cross her station keeping,
Stood the mournful Mother weeping,
Close to Jesus to the last:
Through her heart, his sorrow sharing,
All his bitter anguish bearing,
Now at length the sword had pass’d.

Oh, how sad and sore distress’d
Was that Mother highly blest
Of the sole-begotten One!
Christ above in torment hangs;
She beneath beholds the pangs
Of her dying glorious Son.

Is there one who would not weep,
Whelm’d in miseries so deep
Christ’s dear Mother to behold?
Can the human heart refrain
From partaking in her pain,
In that Mother’s pain untold?

Bruis’d, derided, curs’d, defil’d,
She beheld her tender Child
All with bloody scourges rent;
For the sins of his own nation,
Saw Him hang in desolation,
Till his Spirit forth He sent.

O thou Mother! fount of love!
Touch my spirit from above,
Make my heart with thine accord:
Make me feel as thou hast felt;
Make my soul to glow and melt
With the love of Christ my Lord.

Holy Mother! pierce me through;
In my heart each wound renew
Of my Saviour crucified:
Let me share with thee His pain,
Who for all my sins was slain,
Who for me in torments died.

Let me mingle tears with thee,
Mourning Him who mourn’d for me,
All the days that I may live:
By the Cross with thee to stay;
There with thee to weep and pray;
Is all I ask of thee to give.

Virgin of all virgins best!
Listen to my fond request:
Let me share thy grief divine;
Let me, to my latest breath,
In my body bear the death
Of that dying Son of thine.

Wounded with his every wound,
Steep my soul till it hath swoon’d
In his very blood away;
Be to me, O Virgin, nigh,
Lest in flames I burn and die,
In his awful Judgment day.

Christ, when Thou shalt call me hence,
Be thy Mother my defence,
Be thy Cross my victory;
While my body here decays,
May my soul thy goodness praise,
Safe in Paradise with Thee.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Sacrificia, quae sumpsimus, Domine Jesu Christe, Transfixionem Matris tuae
et Virginis devote celebrantes: nobis impetrent apud clementiam tuam omnis
boni salutaris effectum: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre in unitate.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Own-appointment historical witness. Complete petitions agree under declared typography and the separately recorded spelling pairs, if any; actual Latin conclusions are prefixes of the same own-book family who-livest, with person second-person-direct-address-to-God-the-Son. translations.text: May the sacrifices of which we have partaken, O Lord Jesus Christ, devoutly celebrating the piercing of Thy virgin Mother's soul, obtain for us with Thy clemency the effect of every salutary benefit. Who livest.
